Design points interpreted rather than followed (later steps rely on these):
1. LoopsService has only contribute. The design's interface also has emit, listens, recordRun, attachable, acceptProposal, staleEntries, timeoutEntries; the row cannot implement those without an inbox, a run record and the agreement path, and a stub would be dead code. Same precedent as RulesService. FEAT-011 adds emit/listens/recordRun (+ LoopEventInput, EmitResult, ListedRun types) to service.ts and the provided object; the reader checks only existing members, so adding members does not break it. The service is provided with plain ctx.provide; FEAT-011 moves it into ctx.inject(['sessionController']).
2. "plugin: plainWordsIn empty" (FEAT text) is read with design 3.2: a title or why with a word from PLAIN_WORDS is accepted and shown, and the row health says "<id> 的说法里有 <词>" once. The M7-shaped table in the test has no such word.
3. An entry may name an event nobody declares (design 3.2 last row). Implemented as: validateEntry gets context.absent (plugin only), the registry computes it as the entry's events that are not in the table, not dropped in the same hand-over, and not in loops./gate. (loops. events are always in the table, gate. is refused). The entry is accepted as 'waiting' (greyed, never runs); the parts checkable now are checked (event count, the declared events' filter keys and placeholders). Every contribute/dispose re-checks all held hand-overs against the others (settle), so an entry whose event arrives and does not fit it is dropped then and told to the row health; withdrawing the declaring hand-over greys it again. ContributeResult.accepted/dropped is read after that settle. entries() reasons name events by id and package label by namespace (hourness./env./graph. -> 项目编排, channel. -> GLM 通道); the human title of an undeclared event is not known, so the page step may want to remember titles.
4. Namespace of a hand-over = the namespace of its first valid entry id, else first action, else first event; the execution row (row id glm-hourness/execute) may also use hourness. for events; loops only for row glm-hourness/loops; channel for nobody; gate for row glm-hourness/rules, events only (its entries are dropped, and gate. events from any other row refuse the whole hand-over). Ownership is by (plugin,row) key, released on dispose. A rejected hand-over leaves the earlier one of the same source standing. Design 3.2 lists two ok:false cases (source, namespace); this adds the reserved ones from its namespace row. A contribution whose events/entries/actions is not a list is treated as empty with one dropped record (id 'entries' etc.), not ok:false.
5. A hand-over that lists actions but has no run: all its actions are dropped (design 3.1 says run is required then), so harness entries naming them are dropped too. Entries with scope 'machine' are dropped by the registry (design: only for channel entries, which come through channel.ts); validateEntry itself accepts 'machine' for origin plugin.
6. Bounds the design does not state, chosen here: self.does 1-500 code points; check.tool and check.check 1-200; event title 1-60; action title 1-60; params at most 16; note 1-500 may be multi-line. title is measured after trimming and stored as given (the person path should trim when it writes). to: 'event-session' is accepted only on an event trigger (the design says only events whose envelope has a session, which the declarations do not say).
7. Not enforced in validateEntry because they need the file system or other blocked code: loops.file-changed path is an existing directory and at most 20 per project; check.tool names a graph node; commandText(argv) <= 4000 (script.ts is blocked); script file contents match sha256. The ScriptRef shape (file = docs/loops/scripts/<id>.<ps1|mjs|py|sh>, sha256 64 lowercase hex, lang) is checked.
8. loops.peak-end: the row lists the harness action and a run that answers {outcome:'skipped', reason:'高峰结束时的接续这一版还没有做'}. FEAT-013 replaces the run (peak.ts); FEAT-011's harness executor will call it and get 'skipped' until then. The design says entries 13 and 14 appear only when the pricing service is there; defaults are contributed unconditionally (the pricing coupling comes with channel.ts), and both are greyed anyway because channel.peak-changed is declared by nobody. Only loops.remind-waiting is active today; loops.deps-after-merge turns active when a hand-over declares hourness.trunk-advanced and hourness.outside-advance with a paths-filterable files field.
9. Event keys: hostRestartedKey takes the project key as a parameter (the caller decides what it is); fileChangedKey writes size 'gone' with the last seen mtime; waitingOnHumanKey formats the hour with Intl in the zone given (a bad zone name throws RangeError, the caller passes the host's own zone).
10. rev uses canonicalJson from src/rules/model.ts (a loops -> rules import; no cycle, lint boundary allows it). FEAT-010's store will need the same function; moving it to src/shared/ is a small refactor best done at merge, not done here.
11. 'loops' is in ACTIVATION_ONLY (health.ts): the board is the project's, not a session's, so /hourness-status shows its activation state instead of "已加载，本会话未触发". A later step that reports per session (FEAT-012) should take it out.
12. Dates in docs use the machine clock, 2026-11-01.

Not built, as the plan says: channel.ts and anything importing src/shared/channel-loop.ts, attachDigest and the proposal members, emit/listens/recordRun, storage, inbox, runner, DSH schedule binding, tools, commands, projection, page. package-lock.json stays untracked in the worktree, never committed.
Notes for FEAT-010 and later: LoopEntry has only the plugin source; the person source {kind:'person', at, via, relay, question?, proposal} and status 'active'|'deleted' arrive with the store (widen the union in model.ts). validateEntry already validates a person's entry end to end (script reference included) for the store's read and for loop_propose. The registry is in-memory only and exposes entries()/events() for the page and the runner; the provided service exposes contribute only. Knip counts exports used only by specs as used, but an exported type nobody imports is a finding: keep new exported types imported somewhere.
